Subject: Residency / pinning ask + backup hop authorization

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited about the performance numbers. Before we proceed to a contract, our security and legal teams need a clear commitment on two items related to data residency and cross-region processing:

1) Regional pinning: We need an operational guarantee that customer data for EU-scoped workloads will be pinned to EU region for processing and storage. Please confirm the exact scope (in-flight processing, KV caches, persistent logs).

2) Temporary backup/failover hop: We understand there are scenarios where short-lived cross-region processing is required (e.g., disaster failover, cold replication). We need a defined maximum window for such hops and an approval workflow. Specifically:
   - Maximum duration per incident (hours)
   - Notification and authorization recipients
   - Subprocessor visibility for the backup path

Practical asks:
- A one-page operational statement we can attach to our DPA (or a proposed DPA addendum).
- Current subprocessor roster for the EU and any transient cloud partners used for replication.
- Any SOC 2 / penetration test references you can share.
- An ops runbook or checklist that shows how Redwood handles a failover and how/when data crosses borders.

Can you loop in legal and ops on your side and send an initial proposal by EOD Wednesday (Aug 31)? Appreciate it.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedTech Partners

Ellen / Jordan — legal here. Thanks for the clear ask. High-level comments and requested language below.

Please treat this as our proposed DPA addendum language (summary + required clauses):
1) Residency commitment: Redwood shall ensure that all customer content and derived artifacts for EU-scoped customers are processed and stored in Redwood's EU region. Processing includes inference compute, KV cache population, and persistent logs that contain or are derived from customer content.

2) Temporary Cross-Region Processing: Redwood may permit temporary cross-region processing solely for the purposes of disaster recovery, failover testing, or forced evacuations. Such processing shall be limited to a maximum continuous period of 72 hours per incident unless expressly agreed in writing by the customer. For datasets explicitly marked by the customer as "High Sensitivity", the maximum continuous period shall be 48 hours.

3) Notification and Authorization: Redwood will provide notice to the customer's security contact and contracts email within 2 hours of activation and will publish a post-incident timeline and audit evidence within 10 business days.

4) Subprocessor disclosure: Redwood will maintain an up-to-date subprocessor roster and provide on-request evidence of the transient replication partners used for cross-region hops.

5) Auditability: Redwood shall provide SOC 2 report and a post-activation audit packet (timelines, logs, list of nodes involved) upon reasonable request under NDA.

We also need confirmation whether backup encryption keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed, plus a KMS/escrow option for EU keys. If Redwood can support a customer-controlled key path, include steps and limitations.

Ellen — does this align with what you need? If yes we'll open a DPA addendum draft and circulate via DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Hi all — ops/infra chiming in with practical timelines and runbook notes.

Appended below is an excerpt from ops-pin-playbook.md (attached) — kept short for thread: 

- Activation conditions: Disaster, region-wide outage, or customer-triggered emergency.
- Scope of hop: KV cache warm-up + inference processing on read-only replica. No write-back to customer primary ingest during hop.
- Maximum continuous hop duration: 72 hours (48h for high-sensitivity tag). We recommend tolerating 72h for availability-critical customers but will mark data classes with customer input.
- Notifications: Ops will open incident, tag region-hop, and send automated notice to customer security + contracts within 1 hour of manual activation. (We can reduce to 2 hours if legal prefers — Laura suggested 2 hours in the DPA language; ops prefers 1 hour operationally.)
- Telemetry & logs: We retain activation logs, node IDs, and request traces for 180 days by default; we can produce a focused export for audit within 10 business days.

Planned schedule for deliverables (ops calendar):
- Wed Aug 31 EOD: one-page operational statement + runbook stub (already attached by Jordan).
- Thu Sep 1: ops will validate node roster and provide transient subprocessor list (cloud partners used for replication).
- Fri Sep 2: we aim to have a DPA addendum draft ready for review; Laura to confirm legal language.

Notes / constraints:
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys in EU (bring-your-own-key via our KMS integration) but it adds ~3 weeks to onboarding and requires key-rotation SLAs to be mutually agreed.
- For very high-sensitivity datasets we recommend an isolated Dedicated tenant in the EU (no transient cloud replication) — we'll include cost/ops delta in our proposal.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference
